clue.text: Get rid of outside right in scrap

indicators.note: the word for discarding sits outside the letter for right, wrapping it

parts.note: to shed something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone discards an outside-right player, perhaps from a football team sheet, as so much scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SHED around R. 'outside right' looks like a football position, but the words split: one is the container signal, the other the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment, as in not a shred of evidence.

clue.text: Make notes about coach taxing

indicators.note: the singing word goes about, or around, the coaching word

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Writing notes about a coach journey proves a taxing chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' reads as a bus but is the verb, and 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining work is effortful and demanding, just as taxing work is.

clue.text: Competitions involving lots of people

explanation.surface: Contests that draw in big crowds of entrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are speed contests; races are also large groups of humanity sharing descent, so 'lots of people' in a loose sense.

clue.text: Pointed agitation to restrict the French expenditure

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the shuffled letters close around the French article
agitation stirs up the letters of the word before it into a new order

parts.note: le is the French masculine for 'the'

explanation.surface: A sharp campaign by protesters aims to curb French spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' rearranges the seven letters of 'Pointed', and 'to restrict' wraps them round the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Depletion is the using up of a resource, which is what spending does to funds.

clue.text: Criticise the players and spectators set about one!

indicators.note: the two words are set about, placed around, the numeral

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
the gate is the number of spectators at a match
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Actors and audience round on someone to criticise them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' in the surface means attack, which suits the definition; here it is the container signal. A gate, the crowd at a sports match, is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, a strong synonym for criticising.

clue.text: Learn about borders —- colour's what's needed

indicators.note: the studying word wraps about the edges word

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
rims are borders or edges

explanation.surface: A tip for painters: study the edges of the canvas to choose a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CON around RIMS. CON meaning to learn or study is archaic but a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red shade, one example of a colour.

clue.text: "O ruddier than the cherry, O — than the berry." (Gay)

definitions.text: "O ruddier than the cherry, O — than the berry." (Gay)

parts.words: "O ruddier than the cherry, O — than the berry." (Gay)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from John Gay's libretto for Handel's Acis and Galatea, where the giant Polyphemus praises Galatea

explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Polyphemus's aria in Acis and Galatea, words by John Gay; the missing comparative pairs with 'ruddier'.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank needs a comparative adjective describing a berry, completing the known line of the aria.

clue.text: Private lodging provided with little hesitation

parts.note: an inn offers lodging
er is the short sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A soldier hesitates briefly when offered a billet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier but is an adjective meaning personal or hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones, kept within rather than shown.

clue.text: He keeps old papers, putting the most important four first

parts.note: arch- as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop or archenemy
IV is four in Roman numerals
1st is the short form of first, here written IST

explanation.surface: A records keeper puts his four key files at the top of the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives IST because 1ST is read with the digit as the letter I, a crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist is the custodian of historical records and documents.

clue.text: Men wanting leader plead to follow

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to sue is to plead or petition, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: Leaderless men beg to be allowed to fall in behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting leader' drops the M of MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards as a result, which is to follow on.

clue.text: Welcome absorbing exercise, being quick-witted

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the welcoming word takes in the exercise letters

parts.note: to receive guests is to welcome them
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A bright pupil welcomes the chance to do some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' is the container signal; 'Welcome' looks like a greeting but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptive mind is quick to take in ideas, so alert and sharp.

clue.text: Cuts in police stations

explanation.surface: Budget reductions hit local police stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicks are small cuts or notches; in British slang a nick is also a police station.

clue.text: Publication for children

explanation.surface: A magazine aimed at young readers.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a periodical; in legal and formal language issue means offspring.

clue.text: Gloomy Pole has a spell in the Orient

parts.note: S is the south pole
a turn is a spell or stint
taken as written
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A melancholy Polish man takes a holiday in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it stands for a compass pole, here S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means sullen and morose, from the astrological influence of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: A countryman in a rain storm

indicators.note: a storm whips things about, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A villager caught out in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges IN A RAIN. 'countryman' suggests a rural type, but here it means a native of a particular country.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Iran is one example of a person belonging to a country.

clue.text: A marathon team standing by?

parts.note: marathon as an adjective means very long
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Is a running squad waiting on the start line?
explanation.walkthrough: 'marathon' is used as an adjective meaning lengthy, not the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beside something is to be standing next to it, close at hand.

clue.text: Carrying on operating as a fence

explanation.surface: A busy fence keeps going.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing is ranting or complaining loudly, informally carrying on; a railing is a barrier of bars.

clue.text: Spiritless for a time in an upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval turns things over, so the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone feels deflated for a while during a time of turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' rearranges the letters of A TIME IN AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate is lifeless, lacking any vital spark.

clue.text: A killer and degenerate admitted to an order

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the decay word goes into the knighthood word

parts.note: the Order of the Garter is the senior English order of knighthood
to rot is to degenerate or decay

explanation.surface: A murderer and a reprobate are made knights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' is the container signal. The Order of the Garter is Britain's oldest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotter strangles victims with a cord or wire, so is a kind of murderer.

clue.text: Mature crew accepting directions

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the band word takes in the compass letters

parts.note: a group is a crew or band
W and N are the compass directions west and north

explanation.surface: A seasoned ship's crew takes orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions but means compass points; 'accepting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up person is an adult, fully developed.

clue.text: Outer wear for the white youngster only?

parts.note: pale means white or wan
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Is this coat only for the pale-faced toddler?
explanation.walkthrough: The playful question mark admits the charade is a whimsical split of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose overcoat, a garment worn over other clothing.

clue.text: Making threats to split

indicators.note: making suggests building something new out of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: Someone issues threats to break up a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' rearranges THREATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces, to split apart.

clue.text: Given guidance about entering a horse

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the concerning word goes into the horse word

parts.note: a steed is a horse
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Advice given on whether to enter a horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering a horse' sounds like a race entry; 'entering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be steered is to be directed or guided along a course.

clue.text: Game beauty toting a gun

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the beauty word carries the gun inside

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A gangster's moll: a pretty woman carrying a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toting' is the container signal; 'Game' is the definition, not a hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game of rolling balls into pins and holes.

clue.text: Degree award in the North-west

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
a cup is an award or trophy

explanation.surface: A graduate wins a prize somewhere in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: BACUP is a small town in Lancashire in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a Lancashire mill town, a place located in the North-west of England.

clue.text: The state is a subject for debate

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: The nation itself is a topic for argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a country but is Maine, abbreviated ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a topic or subject for discussion.

clue.text: Some school girls returning home

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the run of letters is read backwards
some means part of, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Several schoolgirls are on their way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks OOLGI from schOOL GIrls, and 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped snow dwelling, an Inuit shelter.

clue.text: Bent, but made some advance, having a heart

indicators.note: having means holding, so the loan word holds a letter
heart says the letter sits at the middle of the loan word

parts.note: lent means advanced money as a loan

explanation.surface: A stooped figure who has lent money out of kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a heart' puts A at the centre of LENT. 'made some advance' looks like progress but means lent money.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so inclined or bent over.

clue.text: Agree with a man in the Church

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him is a male pronoun, a man

explanation.surface: A clergyman sees eye to eye with a parishioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'a man in the Church' suggests a cleric but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime with something is to be in harmony with it, to concur.

clue.text: Call silver worker a loud-mouthed bully

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone names a silversmith as a loud bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver worker' reads as a silversmith but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing, scolding person.

clue.text: Aired in advance, so blocked

parts.note: pre- as a prefix means beforehand
vented means aired, as views are vented or aired

explanation.surface: Grievances were aired beforehand, so the plan was stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance' gives a prefix placed before the airing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevented means stopped or hindered, so blocked.

clue.text: Possibly ten royal characters are to register

indicators.note: possibly indicates the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the royal initials

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten royals are due to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN into ENT. ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a name is to record or register it.
